instruction: Make the top bar clock display the day of the week.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully opened GNOME Settings, navigated to Date & Time, opened the timezone map picker, searched for 'London', and changed timezone from HKT (UTC+8) to GMT (UTC+0) in 11 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open GNOME Settings, navigate sidebar sections, interact with Date & Time settings, use timezone map search, select timezone from results, modify system settings
metadata.task_rationale: Agent demonstrated ability to navigate GNOME Settings and modify Date & Time options. Showing weekday in the top bar clock is a related GNOME display setting, requiring the agent to find the appropriate toggle in Settings (likely under Date & Time or a related panel).
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling weekday display in the GNOME top bar clock. Evaluator checks gsettings clock-show-weekday value is 'true'. This tests the agent's ability to find and toggle a GNOME desktop interface setting.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-show-weekday' to check whether weekday display is enabled in the GNOME top bar clock, which is the exact setting the instruction targets.

Metric 'check_include_exclude' correctly checks that the string 'true' is present in the gsettings output. Since gsettings returns 'true' or 'false' as plain text, the substring inclusion check works correctly and unambiguously ('true' is not a substring of 'false').
Expected value is semantically correct: enabling weekday display requires clock-show-weekday to be 'true'.
Complete coverage: the instruction has a single requirement (show weekday in clock) and the evaluator fully verifies it.
No postconfig needed: gsettings reads persistent dconf state, not transient UI state, so the value is always accessible.
